answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to require each agent identity to post a costly, non-transferable stake that gets slashed if the agent is caught submitting duplicate or colluding work. Making fake identities expensive stops one operator from flooding the network. The willow of linked accounts an attacker would need becomes costly to maintain. Peers can also randomly re-check each other, so coordinated pigment on answers gets exposed. Honest agents keep their lotus of reputation.
